newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-HOLDERS AUXERRE PAY HIGH PRICE FOR CUP VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-HOLDERS AUXERRE PAY HIGH PRICE FOR CUP VICTORY.

text.p: Holders Auxerre paid an expensive price for knocking Lens out of the French Cup on penalties at the weekend by having two key players carried off on stretchers.
Auxerre, who won the penalty shoot-out 5-4, had defender Franck Rabarivony and young striker Steve Marlet, carried off during a tense, but dull match which ended in a goalless draw.
Both will be out of action for several weeks. Marlet sprained his left ankle and was to undergo surgery on Monday while Rabarivony suffered an injury to his right knee.

Lens dominated most of the match but were deprived of a goal by brilliant saves from Auxerre keeper Lionel Charbonnier. It was Charbonnier who eventually handed Auxerre their place in the third round by stopping a penalty by Mickael Debeve in the shoot-out.
"We were ready for penalties," said Auxerre trainer Guy Roux. "Before every Cup match, we practice them in training sessions.
"I was confident," he addded. "Just before the shoot-out, I put pressure on the players by shouting at them at bit. I always do that and usually, it works."
Auxerre international midfielder Sabri Lamouchi admitted the match could have gone either way. "But Lens are a good team and we knew what to expect," he said.

The match was one of three clashes between first division clubs. Nice, bottom of the league, scored an uspet by knocking out third-placed Bastia on penalties on Friday and on Saturday Lille beat Lyon 1-0 thanks to a Djezon Boutoille goal in the 69th minute.

Rennes were the only first division side to bow out to a club from a lower division. The team from Brittany, still unbeaten at home in the league this season, lost 1-0 at home to second division Troyes with Stephane Laquait scoring the winner for the visitors in the 59th minute.

Troubled Paris St Germain were made to work hard by third division Fecamp and it was not until the 75th minute that Cyrille Pouget headed them into the lead. Another goal by Julio Cesar Dely Valdes seven minutes later saw the Paris club win 2-0.
Fourth division Clermont-Ferrand became the smallest club still in the competition by knocking out second division Martigues on penalties.
There are 10 first division clubs left. The draw for the next round is on Sunday.
